newsitem.title: UK: Pet City, PETsMART to merge.
newsitem.headline: Pet City, PETsMART to merge.

text.p: British pet store operator Pet City Holdings Plc and U.S.-based PETsMART Inc said on Friday they agreed to a recommended merger that valued Pet City at about 150.2 million stg.
The deal valued each Pet City share at about 594p, the companies said in a joint statement released here.

Pet City shares closed at 340p in London on Thursday, while PETsMART ended at $29-3/8 in the U.S. Under the terms of the transaction, a holder of 10,000 Pet City shares would receive 3,214 PETsMART shares.
The plan was expected to become effective by December 18.
PETsMART said it did not expect the merger to be dilutive to earnings for the fiscal year ending February 1.

The companies said the combined group would be the leading U.S. and UK operator of specialty superstores supplying pet food and services, with a current total of 311 stores in the U.S. and 50 in the UK.
"We believe Europe represents a 900 to 1,000 store opportunity," PETsMART said.
Following the merger, Pet City chairman Richard Northcott will join the board of PETsMART as a non-executive director.
Giles Clarke will continue as chief executive of Pet City and be named executive vice president of Europe.
PETsMART said it did not currently expect to pay any cash dividends for the foreseeable future, opting instead to retain earnings for expansion.
Neither PETsMART nor Pet City have declared any cash dividends since their respective listings on Nasdaq and the National Market and London's Alternative Investment Market.
Separately, Pet City reported an operating loss of 1.2 million stg on turnover of $54.5 million stg for the year ended July 27. Comparable year-ago figures were not given.
Pet City said it was confident that its target of having 75 stores in operation would be achieved by July 31, 1997, adding that the number could potentially reach 103.
